title: Tabernacle of Praise — Creative Review 05
lead: Five ways to connect sacred dwelling and praise. Each is tested in monochrome, with its strengths and unresolved readings visible.

directions.title: Sacred Space
directions.name: Open Crossing
directions.idea: Two folded boundaries make one open, cruciform shared interior.
directions.visible: Two unequal faceted silhouettes; a vertical crossing with a broad horizontal room; an open upper interval and a diagonal lower threshold.
directions.meaning: Two folded boundaries hold an open cross-shaped interior. Christian gathering is visible; praise is a quieter association with opening and response.
construction: 256-unit canvas; exterior x30–226 and y26–232. The main vertical interval is 44 units wide and the horizontal crossing is 36 units deep.
Two closed black filled silhouettes. The interior is actual space between contours, with no white cover shapes, strokes, masks or raster artwork.
45-degree lower threshold edges align the opening with the faceted enclosure; a 30-degree upper-right plane creates measured asymmetry. The selected seventh development removes the small lower step.
directions.risk: The dense faceted form can feel institutional; the lower opening may read as a chevron. Praise is less immediate than the Christian sacred-space reading.
directions.smallSize: Rendered and visually checked at true 16, 24, 32 and 64 pixels, in black and reverse. The crossing remains visible at 16 pixels; 24 pixels and above better preserve the diagonal threshold and the distinction between the two boundaries.
directions.longevity: Flat filled geometry, generous intervals and no effect-dependent detail support enduring reproduction. The cross is familiar; the asymmetrical enclosure must earn recognition through consistent use rather than a claim of unprecedented symbolism.

type.edits: Outlined humanist letterforms and shaped kerning soften the dense faceted symbol. The phrase keeps natural line lengths; no enlarged initial or roof bar.
type.license: Original Source Serif 4 under SIL OFL 1.1, retained in assets/fonts/sourceserif4/. No font binary modified. Companion lettering is a review specimen, not a final type system.

evaluation.distinctiveness: Distinct counterform; familiar cross aids recall.
evaluation.nameConnection: Dwelling appears through held space, rather than a literal building.
evaluation.integration: Christian space is clear; praise is the weaker half.
evaluation.churchSuitability: Most immediate Christian cue among the symbolic directions.
evaluation.craft: Clean thresholds and related facets; dark mass remains heavy.
evaluation.endurance: Conventional Christian association can endure; distinctive enclosure must earn recognition.
evaluation.smallScale: Cross holds at16; diagonal threshold clearer at24+.
evaluation.monochrome: Strong broad silhouette; no effect-dependent detail.
evaluation.explainability: An open Christian gathering space; do not claim it depicts God.

sketches.name: Open Court
sketches.idea: A canted enclosure surrounds a generous shared interior and leaves diagonal ways through.
sketches.approach: Two turning boundaries; a spatial court rather than a roof illustration.
sketches.reason: The open room is legible, but the split perimeter resembles a generic corporate loop.

sketches.name: Resonant Chamber
sketches.idea: Curved boundaries and an inner shelf test an interior that widens toward its opening.
sketches.approach: Asymmetric curved enclosure with a secondary inward edge.
sketches.reason: The separate inner shelf feels added; the resulting form has too many competing readings.

sketches.name: Common Centre
sketches.idea: Three inward-turning boundaries imply one shared centre without drawing individuals.
sketches.approach: Faceted, separated walls organized around a common interval.
sketches.reason: The gathering is understandable, but the three-part circulation suggests recycling or a business network.

sketches.name: Joined Thresholds
sketches.idea: Two folded boundaries give the shared interior a cruciform shape and leave it open to its surroundings.
sketches.approach: Carve the crossing first; let its upper and lower thresholds determine the surrounding silhouettes.
sketches.reason: The Christian and spatial readings become visible in one construction. This has a clearer reason to exist than the earlier loops.

directions.title: Dwelling and Expression
directions.name: Passing Shelter
directions.idea: A sheltering surface turns inward around a shared interval, then passes outward in uplift.
directions.visible: One broad sweep, an integral lower return, and a rising continuation separated by an open over-under cut.
directions.meaning: Passing surfaces make a sheltered interval and release upward through the same construction. Gathering and expression belong to the same fold.
construction: A broad curved surface shelters the long interior interval and turns back into its lower boundary; the return is integral, with a softened left bend rather than a detached crescent.
A rising continuation passes behind the main sweep. Its 45-degree cut keeps the crossing visibly open rather than relying on a tangent pinch.
The two lower terminals use related 105-degree cuts. Nineteen path anchors describe the black proposal, with no strokes, masks, filters or raster elements.
directions.risk: Wave, bird, or folded fabric can lead before dwelling. The held interval needs enough scale to be understood as a shared place.
directions.smallSize: Rendered and inspected at native 16, 24, 32 and 64 pixels in black and reverse. At 24 pixels the return, shared interval and rising continuation remain distinct. At 16 pixels the silhouette and uplift survive, while the interior compresses and the bird or wave reading strengthens. Use 24 pixels or larger when the spatial idea matters.
directions.longevity: The monochrome silhouette and broad planes avoid dependence on effects or fine detail. Long-term suitability depends on whether the congregation finds the material gesture sufficiently specific to its identity.

type.edits: Calm open sans letterforms give the passing gesture room. Shaped spacing and equal-size name lines preserve a clear, welcoming reading.
type.license: Original Instrument Sans under SIL OFL 1.1, retained in assets/fonts/instrumentsans/. No font binary modified.

evaluation.distinctiveness: Most gestural silhouette; broad crossing is distinct within this set.
evaluation.nameConnection: The sheltered interval connects the fold to dwelling.
evaluation.integration: The same surfaces hold and release; meaning stays abstract.
evaluation.churchSuitability: Warm and expressive, with weaker independent church recognition.
evaluation.craft: Integrated return improves the earlier detached ribbon; cut junctions need proofing.
evaluation.endurance: Avoids trend effects, but wave/bird associations need a reader test.
evaluation.smallScale: Silhouette holds tiny;24+ better for the held interval.
evaluation.monochrome: Expressive without color; central space does real work.
evaluation.explainability: Gathering makes a shelter and turns outward in response.

sketches.name: Opening Offering
sketches.idea: An enclosing wall turns upward at its opening, so the shelter itself begins to lift.
sketches.approach: A continuous curved enclosure with two rising terminals.
sketches.reason: Rejected. The construction remains a generic U, cup or open ring; optical polishing cannot supply the missing distinction.

sketches.name: Breathing Court
sketches.idea: The roof of a shared place turns outward as the room opens.
sketches.approach: A square court with an extended, lifting upper boundary.
sketches.reason: Rejected. The room is legible, but the result resembles an app container or folder; the moving corner does too little expressive work.

sketches.name: Common Bearing
sketches.idea: Two counter-moving surfaces meet around a common interval.
sketches.approach: Broad transverse bands with a central crossing.
sketches.reason: Rejected. The familiar bow-tie or infinity construction supplies movement but does not establish a convincing sheltered space.

sketches.name: Passing Shelter
sketches.idea: A sheltering surface turns inward around a shared interval, then passes outward in uplift.
sketches.approach: An integrated returning fold and an upper continuation crossing over one another.
sketches.reason: Developed. The return belongs to the same sheltering surface, while the crossing gives the whole a distinct outward gesture. Broad planes offer more expressive character than the earlier ring and box constructions.

parts.label: Rising continuation at the passing cut

directions.title: Contemporary Ecclesiastical Emblem
directions.name: The Joined Roundel
directions.idea: An open enclosing roundel holds crafted T and P forms whose lower returns join its base.
directions.visible: An interrupted circle, a broad T, and a P with an open returning tail. The top opening and the P counter remain deliberate negative spaces.
directions.meaning: An open roundel holds crafted T and P initials. Enclosure and a returning letter contour connect dwelling with the name’s response of praise.
construction: A 256-unit canvas contains an open outer roundel; its main body is approximately 18 units thick.
The T and P are independent original paths. Their lower tails overlap the ring at its base; the ring is not one continuous stroke made entirely from the initials.
V2 opened the counters and calmed the T terminal. V3 smooths only the P stem-to-tail junction; the earlier constructions remain preserved.
directions.risk: The roundel and initials may suggest a university, heritage institution, or luxury identity. Its ring can feel decorative rather than essential.
directions.smallSize: Actual black/reverse tests: the silhouette persists at 16px, but TP reading and lower gaps are unreliable. 24px is marginal; 32px is the more credible symbol test, with 48px clearer. Complete lockups remain readable at 320px and 240px; those widths do not establish a print minimum.
directions.longevity: The one-color roundel and restrained letter contrast have durable precedents, but the heritage associations must be accepted deliberately. Its fine counter relationships need production proof before any small physical use.

type.edits: A restrained open sans companion balances the more inscribed TP emblem. It reduces the double heritage emphasis of an ornate symbol plus a serif name.
type.license: Original Instrument Sans under SIL OFL 1.1, retained in assets/fonts/instrumentsans/. The TP symbol is separately drawn original artwork; no font binary modified.

evaluation.distinctiveness: Crafted initials give a memorable formal identifier; roundels are familiar.
evaluation.nameConnection: T and P directly identify Tabernacle and Praise.
evaluation.integration: Enclosure and return relate, but ring and letters remain separate contours.
evaluation.churchSuitability: Dignified ecclesial character, with a strong heritage tone.
evaluation.craft: Resolved letter junctions and open counters; fine T/P separation needs care.
evaluation.endurance: Traditional inscription language is relatively durable, though not uniquely church-like.
evaluation.smallScale: TP reads best at32+; tiny initials and reverse crowd.
evaluation.monochrome: Works as a flat emblem; color is not carrying it.
evaluation.industryRisk: University, heritage institution, or luxury monogram.
evaluation.explainability: The parish initials held in a shared enclosing form.

sketches.name: Common Bond
sketches.idea: A close-set TP monogram gives the parish initials a broad sheltering crossbar and an upward-cut return.
sketches.approach: Letter-led emblem: drawn contrast, a generous P counter, and restrained calligraphic terminals.
sketches.reason: Clearer initials, but the silhouette is less memorable and can resemble a conventional luxury monogram.

sketches.name: Response Medallion
sketches.idea: The P returns around the T to establish an enclosing circular emblem.
sketches.approach: In this initial construction the returning P also supplies the eastern edge of the open roundel.
sketches.reason: The strongest emblem silhouette. Its first lower junction was crowded; development separated the enclosing contour from the letter tails to improve reading.

sketches.name: Coupled Banner
sketches.idea: Two folded panels join around an upright interior seam.
sketches.approach: A textile-led emblem with no initials: paired panels, a shared crown, and a narrow central opening.
sketches.reason: A distinct non-letter alternative, but its closed mass can resemble a shield, book, or ceremonial badge and feels less welcoming.

directions.title: Custom Typographic Identity
directions.name: Open Counter
directions.idea: A full-name wordmark links dwelling and praise through held counters and repeated upward release inside the letters.
directions.visible: A normal-proportioned T, a P with a rising counter floor, custom double-storey a forms, sloped e bars, and outward r/f terminals. These six original glyph designs repeat through eleven of the eighteen letters in the complete name.
directions.meaning: Enclosed bowls and rising counter floors repeat across the actual letters. The complete name carries the identity through one consistent letter grammar.
construction: Six letter designs—T, P, a, e, r, and f—are original drawn contours. The seven other glyphs b/c/l/n/o/i/s remain unchanged licensed Source Serif 4 outlines at weight 550 and optical size 24.

P/a/e counters and r/f terminals repeat a rising or outward-cut movement. Pair-specific spacing keeps the two words readable; T stays within ordinary cap proportions and never spans the name as a roof.

V2 strengthened the rising P/e counter floors, opened a/e exits, and gave f the same non-ball terminal rule. V3 adds 40 units of top canvas padding to prevent inherited b/l ascender clipping; all V2 letter geometry and spacing are preserved.
directions.risk: The familiar serif base can feel editorial or bookish. Custom details are restrained and do not make the Christian association explicit without the name.
directions.smallSize: Actual 320px and 240px full-name tests are readable in black and reverse in both layouts. The stacked form preserves far more letter detail at these widths. The horizontal form is intentionally long, and its custom details become less evident at 240px. The complete name is not claimed to read at 16px; very small avatars remain unresolved.
directions.longevity: Familiar serif word shapes support long-term reading, while the repeated custom details avoid relying on a fashionable symbol. Fine terminal cuts will need physical-size proofs before embroidery, engraving, or small print use.

type.family: Source Serif 4, weight 550 / optical size 24, with six original letter drawings
type.edits: Original drawn T/P/a/e/r/f replace those glyphs in the outlined logo artwork. Unchanged licensed b/c/l/n/o/i/s remain visibly part of the design. Optical pair spacing is adjusted. The font binary itself is not edited, and this is not claimed as a wholly original typeface. The D2 sketch separately uses Instrument Sans plus original T/P/a and trial ligatures; D3 uses an original drawn capital alphabet.
type.license: Source Serif 4 and Instrument Sans: SIL Open Font License 1.1. Unmodified originals and licenses are retained in assets/fonts/sourceserif4/ and assets/fonts/instrumentsans/ within this review. The builder uses these portable assets first, with a prior-study fallback. No font files were modified.

evaluation.distinctiveness: Distinctive repeated counter grammar; overall voice remains familiar serif.
evaluation.nameConnection: The complete name gives the clearest verbal identification.
evaluation.integration: Dwelling/response are expressed inside real letterforms, subtly.
evaluation.churchSuitability: Appropriate dignified name; faith association relies on words and RCCG context.
evaluation.craft: Six originally drawn letters and optical pair spacing; no oversize T.
evaluation.endurance: Familiar letter structures support enduring reading; editorial tone is a decision.
evaluation.smallScale: Full name tested320/240 wide; no 16px avatar claim.
evaluation.monochrome: The wordmark stands without a badge, color, or mockup.
evaluation.industryRisk: Book imprint, editorial identity, or cultural organization.
evaluation.explainability: The name itself shares a held-and-opening letter grammar.

sketches.name: Open Counter
sketches.idea: Give the complete name a repeatable grammar of contained interior space and rising release.
sketches.approach: Original T/P/a/e/r letter drawings sit within a Source Serif 4 word skeleton; the repeated a/e/r details make the treatment visible across both principal words.
sketches.reason: The best balance of word recognition, warmth, and identity-specific letter craft. It warranted a more consistent counter and terminal system.

sketches.name: Joined Voices
sketches.idea: The na and ra pairs connect through a shared baseline movement.
sketches.approach: Original T/P/a drawings and trial ligatures are combined with licensed Instrument Sans outlines.
sketches.reason: The literal joining makes the collective idea visible, but darkens the name and weakens the distinction between r/a and n/a. It is an exploratory alternative, not a recommended compact mark.

sketches.name: Inscribed Response
sketches.idea: An original incised capital alphabet gives both words an enduring ceremonial rhythm.
sketches.approach: Every displayed letter is drawn from a common cap-height, wedge-terminal, and chamfered-counter system.
sketches.reason: The most fully bespoke alphabet, but the monumental tone is cooler and can suggest a museum, university, or cultural foundation.

directions.title: Cadenced Wall Reimagined
directions.name: Opening Measure
directions.idea: A single folded wall enlarges its openings as it turns around a shared interior; the dwelling itself supplies the cadence.
directions.visible: A joined sloping surface, two measured cuts and one generous interior open through the lower edge. Angular left faces answer a curved outer return.
directions.meaning: One joined architectural face enlarges its openings as it turns. Cadence comes from changing openness within the dwelling, rather than separate rising buildings.
construction: One upper diagonal joins every zone. The two cuts sit below it with substantial material bridges instead of dividing the mark into separate pillars.
Small intervals lead toward a larger shared interior. The lower threshold is genuinely open, replacing v3’s pinched point contact.
Angular folded faces on the left contrast with a broad curved return on the right. All cuts are real negative space in one filled compound path.
directions.risk: A sculptural property or product emblem remains possible. The large interior can still suggest a flame; finer cadence weakens at tiny sizes.
directions.smallSize: Native 16 px retains the sloping silhouette and open interior, while the finer upper interval largely merges. At 24 px the folded structure is identifiable; at 32 px the measured cuts are clearer. White reverse retains the threshold but looks slightly heavier at tiny sizes. Use 32 px or larger when the full cadence matters.
directions.longevity: The identity rests on a structural silhouette and the relationship of solid to space, without a transient effect. Long-term usefulness is plausible, but church warmth and the sculptural/property association need congregation review.

type.edits: Humanist counters add warmth beside the angular architecture. The complete name anchors a mark that would otherwise resemble a cultural or property emblem.
type.license: Original Source Serif 4 under SIL OFL 1.1, retained in assets/fonts/sourceserif4/. No font binary modified.

evaluation.distinctiveness: Strong joined diagonal mass; different from the earlier skyline.
evaluation.nameConnection: A wall becomes a shared interior, rather than separate buildings.
evaluation.integration: Changing openings supply cadence inside the architecture.
evaluation.churchSuitability: Church meaning is indirect; full name remains essential.
evaluation.craft: Real bridges and open lower threshold repair earlier fragile joins.
evaluation.endurance: Structural silhouette can endure; property association remains unresolved.
evaluation.smallScale: Full cadence best32+; finer cut merges at16.
evaluation.monochrome: One mass and its cuts work in pure black and reverse.
evaluation.industryRisk: Sculptural property, product, or cultural identity.
evaluation.explainability: One dwelling opens progressively into collective response.

sketches.name: Returning Court
sketches.idea: A folded perimeter turns around a common court; its increasing depth becomes the expression.
sketches.approach: Plan-like enclosing fold with open entrance
sketches.reason: Gathered interior is visible. A cog, wreath or enclosing fortress remains possible; the tapering seams are too complex for a lead mark.

sketches.name: One Fold
sketches.idea: One strip folds around an interior and then rises beyond its own enclosure.
sketches.approach: Continuous folded ribbon
sketches.reason: One continuous object carries dwelling and movement. The interlocking corners can read as packaging, recycling or a technology loop.

sketches.name: Answering Surfaces
sketches.idea: Two folded surfaces answer across one shared interior; each helps make the room.
sketches.approach: Interdependent solid and counterform
sketches.reason: Large counter and directional weight are clear. At first glance it may be an abstract leaf pair, split flame or rotational industry mark.

sketches.name: Opening Measure
sketches.idea: A stable architectural mass progressively opens, so its own structure becomes generous.
sketches.approach: Carved mass with opening intervals
sketches.reason: The carved mass has a strong edge but the wedge/roof silhouette still suggests contemporary property or a sculptural building.

sketches.name: Processional Fold
sketches.idea: A horizontal gathering becomes one broad rising return, expressing praise through movement.
sketches.approach: Low pleated procession and rising sweep
sketches.reason: The sweep is kinetic and changes the axis of the original. Jagged peaks can suggest mountains, a sports brand or an upward chart.

sketches.name: Common Vault
sketches.idea: Unequal folded shells join around one interior rather than stand as individual pillars.
sketches.approach: Sculptural enclosing shell
sketches.reason: The most unified shell construction, with cadence around a room. Could read as a folded rosette, aperture or abstract flame; avoid overclaiming immediate church recognition.

rccg.note: The repository records a user-supplied RCCG PNG and its checksum, but the actual image file is still absent. This is a labeled reservation only; no emblem is reconstructed. Actual emblem balance and publication authorization remain unverified.

sources.title: Scriptural sources and interpretation limits
sources.note: Exact passages distinguish sacred dwelling, praise, and current design interpretations.

assessment: C is the most resolved emblematic construction, and D provides the clearest name recognition. Neither is automatically the best parish identity: C risks heritage/luxury associations, while D remains editorial and its custom character is restrained.

A has the most immediate Christian association, but its dark mass still needs a warmth test. B has the most expressive gesture, with the least secure church reading. E is the most substantial architectural rethinking: keep it active, while testing its sculptural/property association and tiny cuts.

E received more exploration because the brief requested it. The developed comparison uses the same area, backgrounds, full names, size proofs, and applications for all five. No direction, palette, type system, or publishing template is approved.
